summary: For every finite M, already for A=I_3 there are fixed second/third marginals with at most M interval components and a target interval such that the exact one-coordinate bathtub optimum for the first marginal requires more than M separated support components. Hence the completed coordinatewise extreme-product localization cannot be strengthened to a universal fixed fragment-count cap while preserving each fixed-fiber optimum. This does not refute the global QFORM conjecture or globally rule out an M-fragment extremality theorem by a different non-coordinatewise mechanism.
